sections.content:
Kelkoo Sales Tracking (KST) helps Kelkoo Group measure the sales generated by your campaigns and optimise the traffic we send to your website.

By providing Kelkoo Group with accurate sales data, KST enables our optimisation algorithms to identify the traffic sources, placements and offers that deliver the best performance for your business.

sections.section_heading: Why is Kelkoo Sales Tracking important?
sections.content:
Kelkoo Sales Tracking records sales completed on your website and provides Kelkoo Group with the information required to measure the performance of your campaigns.

This data allows us to understand which traffic generates the most value for your business and optimise your campaigns accordingly.

For example, KST data helps our optimisation systems determine which:

- traffic sources generate valuable sales;
- placements perform best;
- products and offers should receive more or less traffic.

Accurate and complete sales tracking is therefore essential for effective campaign optimisation.

sections.section_heading: How does Kelkoo Sales Tracking work?
sections.content:
KST uses two main components:

### Lead Tag

The Lead Tag is loaded on your website to identify visits originating from Kelkoo Group.

When the required consent has been obtained, it stores an anonymous identifier using first-party storage. This identifier allows KST to recognise a Kelkoo visit if the user subsequently completes a purchase.

### Conversion Tag

The Conversion Tag fires when an order is completed and sends information about the transaction to Kelkoo Group.

This includes information such as:

- the order ID;
- the order value;
- the Kelkoo identifier, when available;
- additional transaction information, depending on your implementation.

The Conversion Tag should fire for every completed order . Kelkoo Group then determines whether the transaction should be attributed to Kelkoo traffic.

Important KST should track every sale completed on your website, not only sales that you believe were generated by Kelkoo Group. Kelkoo Group applies its own attribution logic to determine which sales should be attributed to Kelkoo traffic. Missing or modified sales data can affect our ability to accurately measure and optimise your campaign performance.

Important

KST should track every sale completed on your website, not only sales that you believe were generated by Kelkoo Group.

Kelkoo Group applies its own attribution logic to determine which sales should be attributed to Kelkoo traffic. Missing or modified sales data can affect our ability to accurately measure and optimise your campaign performance.

Kelkoo Group and Google Analytics attribution Kelkoo Group uses its own attribution methodology. As a result, the number of sales attributed to Kelkoo Group may differ from the figures reported by Google Analytics or other analytics platforms. See How to use your analytics platform to track Kelkoo Group traffic for more information.

Kelkoo Group and Google Analytics attribution

Kelkoo Group uses its own attribution methodology. As a result, the number of sales attributed to Kelkoo Group may differ from the figures reported by Google Analytics or other analytics platforms.

See How to use your analytics platform to track Kelkoo Group traffic for more information.

For a more detailed explanation, see Understanding Kelkoo Sales Tracking .

Kelkoo Sales Tracking has been designed to minimise the amount of data collected and to respect applicable privacy requirements.

### Lead Tag

The Lead Tag requires the appropriate user consent before setting first-party cookies or using equivalent browser storage.

Users are identified using an anonymous identifier.

### Conversion Tag

The Conversion Tag does not require separate user consent. Kelkoo Group relies on legitimate interest as the legal basis for processing the sales data required to measure and optimise campaign performance.

Kelkoo Group only uses sales data relevant to the measurement and optimisation of Kelkoo Group campaigns and does not collect information that directly identifies individual customers.

For complete information about data processing, cookies and your responsibilities as an advertiser, see:

- GDPR Notice for Kelkoo Sales Tracking
- Kelkoo Group Privacy Policy
- Kelkoo Group Cookie Policy

sections.section_heading: How should I install Kelkoo Sales Tracking?
sections.content:
For the most accurate tracking, we recommend implementing both:

- Google Tag Manager (GTM) tracking
- Server-to-server integration

When possible, these methods should run in parallel to maximise tracking coverage and accuracy.

Other installation methods are also available for websites using specific ecommerce platforms or custom technical setups.

See Installation Methods to choose the most appropriate implementation for your website.

Our documentation covers the most common installation methods and troubleshooting scenarios .

If you are unable to resolve an issue after reviewing the installation and troubleshooting guides, contact the Kelkoo Group Support team through your Merchant Center .

Note Technical support is currently provided in English only.

Technical support is currently provided in English only.

pages.page_title: GDPR Notice for Kelkoo Sales Tracking

sections.content:
Kelkoo Sales Tracking uses first-party cookies (in line with industry standards) which are set on your own domain.

In respect of Kelkoo Group traffic sourced from Google, Kelkoo Sales Tracking also calls a Google Global Site Tag to track conversions. The Google Global Site Tag uses cookies to identify unique users.

If you are using Kelkoo Sales Tracking, we suggest that you include the following information (or equivalent) in your cookie policy to notify users.

name | Role | domain name | Duration | Comment
kelkooId | Measurement | your domain | 12 months | The kelkooid is used to mesure the performance of the Kelkoo ad campaigns
kk_gclid | Measurement | your domain | 12 months | The kk_gclid is used to mesure the performance of the Kelkoo Group ad campaigns
kk_leadtag | Technical | your domain | 12 months | The kk_leadtag is used to determine the version of the tracking tool that is used.

More information can be found at https://www.kelkoo.co.uk/company-pages/privacy-policy/ . Please also refer to Google´s cookie policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy?hl=en-US .

sections.content:
Info | Description
Technology partner | Kelkoo Group
Data Host | Kelkoo Group
Country of data storage | The Netherlands
Period of data storage | Raw data with timestamp: Clicks, tracking points and events: Indefinite Impressions: 30 days Aggregated data: Indefinite
List of processed and stored data | User ID Time of Interaction URL of Interaction IP address Location data User agent data Sales transaction data Transaction details (if supplied by merchant)
Description of processed and stored data | Transaction details stored are defined by merchant integration and can include Product Ids, basket value, product names etc

Integration type | Asynchronous JavaScript Tag

Data collected as part of Kelkoo Sales Tracking is processed by Kelkoo Group on its own behalf and Kelkoo Group is responsible as the data controller for the purposes of GDPR.

This is independent of any similar data which may be collected by you on your own behalf (or through other partners you work with), in respect of which you (or your partners) remain data controllers.

There is no controller-processor relationship between Kelkoo Group and You.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact your usual contact at Kelkoo Group, or Kelkoo Group's Data Protection Officer at dpo@kelkoogroup.com .

After installing Kelkoo Sales Tracking, we strongly recommend testing your implementation before considering the setup complete.

See Test your Kelkoo Sales Tracking setup for detailed instructions.

Once Kelkoo Sales Tracking is installed, additional configuration options are available for more advanced implementations.

These include:

- Adding basket information – Share information about the products included in each transaction with Kelkoo Sales Tracking.
- Reimplementing the Lead Tag logic – Implement the Lead Tag functionality yourself when the standard implementation is not suitable.
- Server-to-server integration – Implement sales tracking without relying entirely on browser-side tracking.

Kelkoo Sales Tracking is designed to have minimal impact on your website's performance.

The tracking scripts and requests run asynchronously, allowing the rest of the page to load independently.

Typical timings are:

- Approximately 100 ms to download the Lead Tag (2.9 kB compressed). The download is asynchronous and does not block the page from displaying.
- Approximately 22 ms to download the Sales Tracking tag (3.9 kB compressed).
- Approximately 180 ms for the request to the Kelkoo Sales Tracking service. This request is performed in the background and does not block the user experience.

We recommend loading the script using defer where applicable to further minimise its impact on page loading.

- Add Basket Information
- Lead Tag Reimplementation
- Server to server integration

You can enrich your Kelkoo Sales Tracking (KST) implementation by sending information about the products included in each transaction.

Basket information helps Kelkoo Group better understand which products generate sales and enables additional performance optimisations.

The implementation depends on how you installed Kelkoo Sales Tracking.

If you installed KST manually, add a basket parameter to the _kkstrack variable on your order confirmation page.

The basket parameter must contain an array of all products included in the transaction:

```
_kkstrack = {
  ...
  basket:  [{ productname: 'Man@@ubri ricoperti di spugna 1 kg x 2 pz ',
              productid: '1',
              quantity: '1',
              price: '4.2'
            },
            { productname: 'p2',
              productid: '2',
              quantity: '3',
              price: '8.6'
            },
            ...
            ]
  ...
};
```

All four fields are required for each product:

Field | Description
productname | Name of the product
productid | Unique identifier of the product
quantity | Number of units purchased
price | Unit price of the product

Important The productid should match the product identifier used in your Kelkoo Group offer feed, such as the EAN, SKU or another unique product ID. Using the same identifier allows Kelkoo Group to match transactions with the corresponding products in your feed and enables additional performance optimisations.

Important

The productid should match the product identifier used in your Kelkoo Group offer feed, such as the EAN, SKU or another unique product ID.

Using the same identifier allows Kelkoo Group to match transactions with the corresponding products in your feed and enables additional performance optimisations.

If you installed KST through Google Tag Manager, your Data Layer must contain information about the products included in the transaction.

```
window.dataLayer = window.dataLayer || [];
dataLayer.push({
  'transactionId':'1234',
  'transactionAffiliation':'Acme Clothing',
  'transactionTotal':38.26,
  'transactionTax':1.29,
  'transactionShipping':5,
  'transactionProducts':[{
    'sku':'DD44',
    'name':'T-Shirt',
    'category':'Apparel',
    'price':11.99,
    'quantity':1},
    {
    'sku':'AA345',
    'name':'Boots',
    'category':'Shoes',
    'price':99.99,
    'quantity':4
  }]
})
```

Make sure the product information required by your KST configuration is available in the Data Layer.

Important The sku should match the product identifier used in your Kelkoo Group offer feed, such as the EAN, SKU or another unique product ID. Using consistent identifiers allows Kelkoo Group to match purchased products with the corresponding products in your feed and enables additional performance optimisations.

Important

The sku should match the product identifier used in your Kelkoo Group offer feed, such as the EAN, SKU or another unique product ID.

Using consistent identifiers allows Kelkoo Group to match purchased products with the corresponding products in your feed and enables additional performance optimisations.

``` - Kelkoo Sales Tracking also supports Google Analytics baskets ``` [ { "id": "P12345", "name": "Android Warhol T-Shirt", "list_name": "Search Results", "brand": "Google", "category": "Apparel/T-Shirts", "variant": "Black", "list_position": 1, "quantity": 2, "price": '2.0' }, { "id": "P67890", "name": "Flame challenge TShirt", "list_name": "Search Results", "brand": "MyBrand", "category": "Apparel/T-Shirts", "variant": "Red", "list_position": 2, "quantity": 1, "price": '3.0' } ] ```

This guide is intended for merchants who cannot use the standard Kelkoo Group leadtag.js script and need to reproduce its essential functionality in their own implementation.

For most integrations, we recommend using the standard Kelkoo Lead Tag . Only use the approach described below if you have a specific technical requirement to implement the Lead Tag logic yourself.

The kk URL parameter is automatically added by Kelkoo Group when a user clicks one of your ads.

Your Lead Tag implementation retrieves the value of kk and stores it as kelkooId

### Important

- Installation via Google Tag Manager (GTM) or Manual installation is the official implementation (see Installation Methods).
- This Server-to-Server implementation is only intended as a fallback method to increase tracking coverage.
- It is only available if you have an in-house development team managing. It is not suitable for agency/third party or if you don't have a technical team.
- We don't provide custom implementation and a very limited technical support for this implementation.
- You need to track inbound traffic directly from Kelkoo Group Network, as well as parallel tracking calls when the url contains gclid id from Google
- You need to make sure all sales are tracked, in-session as well as those made on a different session than the initial click.

### Global view

[image: KelkooSalesTrackingS2SSynchrone.png]

- End user browses Kelkoo Group websites, when clicking an offer on Kelkoo Group Network, he is redirected to the merchant website.
- KelkooId ( kk ) and Google Click Id ( gclid ) is passed as parameters of the url

ex: https://www.acme.com/miror/137-miror.html?**kk=a4csscc-1781b717420-34cf3**&**gclid=EAIaIQobChMIpNXu6r6D6AIVQsjeCh27SQXcEAkYAyABEgIhz_D_BwE**&utm_source=kelkoofr&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign=kelkooclick

- When the user reaches one of your Product page, your website stores kk and gclid id in a table on your website's backend, and associate it to the current user via the login/basket

basket | login | kk | gclid
17e8b1bxx7r17420 | 1233443 | a4csscc-1781b717420-34cf3 | EAIaIQobChMIpNXu6r6D6AIVQsjeCh27SQXcEAkYAyABEgIhz_D_BwE
... | ... | ... | ...

- When the user buys the product and reaches your Confirmation Page, your Website retrieves kk and gclid params value from database and calls the Kelkoo Group Sales Tracking Webservice on https://s.kelkoogroup.net/st for each sale with an HTTP GET with the following parameters:

name | type | mandatory | description | example
country | String | true | The 2-letter country code for the country on which your products are listed on Kelkoo Group: | fr
orderId | String | true | A unique order identifier | FAPC-MZL8-QFNY
comId | Long | true | The unique ID representing your shop within the Kelkoo Group system | 100503562
orderValue | Double | true | The total amount of the order | 37.72
productsInfos | String | true | A UrlEncoded Base64 of a Json Array of the products in the basket. | W3sicHJvZHVjdG5hbWUiOiJTaGltYW5vIiwiaWQiOiJwcm9kMTMwODIzIiwicHJpY2UiOjE0Ljk5LCJxdWFudGl0eSI6Mn1d [{"productname":"Shimano","productid":"prod130823","price":14.99,"quantity":2}]
saleId | Double | true | A randomly generated number between 0 and 1 | 0.24603935101497432
kelkooId | String | false | The value of the kk parameter in the url of your landing page | a4c6224-1700767fb9f-c3de3
gclid | String | false | The value of the gclid parameter in the url of your landing page | EAIaIQobChMIpNXu6r6D6AIVQsjeCh27SQXcEAkYAyABEgIhz_D_BwE
msclkid | String | false | The value of the msclkid parameter in the url of your landing page | 751ff8c7d3bf17f6f6729c640c4249d5
returningUser | Boolean | false | "true" if the sale is done by a returning user, "false" for a new user | true
source | String | false | Set this param value to "serverToServer" | serverToServer

Here is an example of decoded and pretty-printed productsInfos :

```
[
  {
    "productname": "Shimano", // string
    "productid": "prod130823", // string
    "price": 14.99, // double
    "quantity": 2 // integer, floating number is not allowed here
  }
]
```

### GDPR considerations

Consent needs to be managed directly by merchants as this is not part of the traditional cookie consent mechanism. See GDPR Notice for Kelkoo Sales Tracking.

sections.section_heading: Before setting up your Kelkoo Sales Tracking Tag
sections.content:
### Get your merchantId and associated Country Code

See How To get your merchantId and associated Country Code

### Clean any old version of Kelkoo Sales Tracking

- In your code, remove any Kelkoo Sales tracking tag (search for leadtag.js and _kkstrack )
- On your website backend, uninstall any Kelkoo Sales Tracking plugin you might have installed

You need to install two elements:

- the Leadtag , in charge of writing the cookie when the user first visits your website
- the Conversion tag , in charge of retrieving data from the cookie and registering the sale

BOTH ARE MANDATORY FOR KELKOO SALES TRACKING TO WORK

### Install the leadtag

Find and edit the right XML layout and add :

```
<reference name="head">
  <block type="core/text" name="kelkoo.lead.tag">
      <action method="setText">
        <text>
          <![CDATA[<script type="text/javascript" src="https://s.kk-resources.com/leadtag.js"></script>]]>
        </text>
      </action>
  </block>
</reference>
```

### Install the conversion tag

- Paste this code at the end of the file . It gets the Order Value and the Order Id mandatory for Kelkoo Sales Tracking to work.

To add in web/app/design/frontend/custom/default/template/checkout/success.phtml , where custom is the name of your template.

```
<?php
  $orderObj = Mage::getModel('sales/order')->loadByIncrementId($this->getOrderId());
  $_totalData =$orderObj->getData();
?>
```

- Right after the code added above, add the Conversion tag.

```
<script type="text/javascript">
  _kkstrack = {
    merchantInfo : [{ country:'COUNTRY_CODE', merchantId:'MERCHANTID_VALUE' }],
    orderValue: '<?=$_totalData['grand_total'] ?>',
    orderId: '<?=$this->getOrderId() ?>',
    basket:  []
  };
  (function() {
    var s = document.createElement('script');
    s.type = 'text/javascript';
    s.async = true;
    s.src = 'https://s.kk-resources.com/ks.js';
    var x = document.getElementsByTagName('script')[0];
    x.parentNode.insertBefore(s, x);
  })();
</script>
```

- You need to edit some elements of the Conversion Tag. Those values can be hardcoded as they are the same for all the sales registered.
- MERCHANTID_VALUE : This is the unique ID representing your shop within the Kelkoo Group system. Check How To get your merchantId and associated Country Code. If you have multiple MerchantId please check If you have multiple merchantIds and countries
- COUNTRY_CODE is the 2-letter country code (lower case) for the country on which your products are listed on Kelkoo Group. Check Full list of Kelkoo Group country codes

### Install the leadtag If you want to add Kelkoo Sales Tracking leadtag without creating a module, you can add the following code on your active theme. To add in YourTheme/Magento_Theme/layout/default_head_blocks.xml ``` ``` - Enable kelkoost module : ``` php bin/magento module:enable Kelkoo_Modulekelkoost php bin/magento setup:upgrade --keep-generated ```
Please check Test Integration

### Backup your files

Before doing any changes, please remember to back up the files you’re going to modify.

### Check Recompile option

- Go to Advanced settings -> Performance
- Make sure option “Recompile files of template if updated” is checked.

- Open the file themes/custom/header.tpl (where custom is the name of your template, the default being “prestashop”)
- Add at the bottom of the file

```
<script async="true" type="text/javascript" src="https://s.kk-resources.com/leadtag.js" ></script>
```

- Clear the cache.

You need to edit some elements of the Conversion Tag

Those values can be hardcoded as they are the same for all the sales registered.

- MERCHANTID_VALUE: This is the unique ID representing your shop within the Kelkoo Group system. Check How To get your merchantId and associated Country Code. If you have multiple MerchantId please check If you have multiple merchantIds and countries
- COUNTRY_CODE is the 2-letter country code (lower case) for the country on which your products are listed on Kelkoo Group. Check Full list of Kelkoo Group country codes

### If you have multiple merchantIds and countries

If you have several Kelkoo Group campaigns running for the same website (multiple MerchantId), you can setup all campaigns within the same tag.

You just need to have the following structure for the merchantInfo variable:

```
merchantInfo : [
  {
    country:'fr',
    merchantId:'12941513'
  },
  {
    country:'uk',
    merchantId:'56789'
  }
]
```

pages.page_title: Installation via Google Tag Manager (GTM) with Enhanced Ecommerce

sections.content: If your website uses Google Tag Manager (GTM), this is the recommended method for installing Kelkoo Sales Tracking (KST).
You can also follow our video tutorial: How to Install KST using GTM

sections.section_heading: Step 1: Identify the Data Layer variables
sections.content:
Before configuring Kelkoo Sales Tracking, you need to identify the Data Layer variables used by your website for purchase events.

### 1.1 Start GTM Preview mode

From your Google Tag Manager workspace, click Preview to launch Tag Assistant.

### 1.2 Connect your website

In the Tag Assistant window, enter your website URL and click Connect .

Make sure the URL belongs to the website on which the relevant GTM container is installed.

### 1.3 Check the connection

Your website should open in a new browser tab.

In Tag Assistant, confirm that the connection status is displayed as Connected .

### 1.4 Complete a test purchase

On the website opened in the previous step, complete a test purchase.

### 1.5 Find the purchase event

Return to Tag Assistant.

In the event list on the left, locate the event corresponding to the order confirmation or thank-you page.

### 1.6 Identify the relevant ecommerce event

Select the event associated with the completed purchase.

The exact event name depends on your website's GTM and Enhanced Ecommerce implementation.

### 1.7 Identify the required values

Open the Data Layer tab and identify the following values:

- Event name
- Order ID
- Order value

For example:

- Event name: purchase
- Order ID: ecommerce.purchase.transaction_id
- Order value: ecommerce.purchase.value

[image: GTM_datalayer_example.png]

Important: Data Layer variables vary from one website to another. The examples above may therefore differ from those used on your website.

If you cannot find equivalent purchase information in the Data Layer, contact your ecommerce platform or implementation provider to check whether Enhanced Ecommerce data is being sent to GTM. Depending on your ecommerce platform, a plugin or extension may also be available to provide the required GTM ecommerce integration.

You now need to create GTM variables for the Order ID and Order Value identified in Step 1.

### 2.1 Open Variables

In your GTM workspace, select Variables from the left-hand menu.

[image: 2.1GTM_variables_menu.png]

### 2.2 Create a new variable

Under User-Defined Variables , click New .

[image: 2.2GTM_variables_menu.png]

### 2.3 Select the variable type

Click Variable Configuration , then select Data Layer Variable .

[image: 2.3GTM_variable_menu.png]

### 2.4 Create the Order ID variable

In Data Layer Variable Name , enter the Order ID variable identified in Step 1.7.

For example:

ecommerce.purchase.transaction_id

Give the variable a clear name, such as Order ID , and save it.

[image: 2.4GTM_variable_menu.png]

### 2.5 Create the Order Value variable

Repeat the previous step using the Order Value variable identified in Step 1.7.

For example:

ecommerce.purchase.value

Give the variable a clear name, such as Order Value , and save it.

sections.section_heading: Step 3: Create a trigger for the purchase event
sections.content:
Next, create a GTM trigger that fires when the purchase event identified in Step 1 occurs.

### 3.1 Open Triggers

From the left-hand menu, select Triggers .

[image: 3.1GTM_event_menu.png]

### 3.2 Create a new trigger

Click New , then click Trigger Configuration .

[image: 3.2.1GTM_event_menu.png]

### 3.3 Select Custom Event

Choose Custom Event as the trigger type.

[image: 3.3GTM_event_menu.png]

### 3.4 Configure the event

In Event name , enter the event name identified in Step 1.7.

For example:

purchase

Configure the trigger to fire on the appropriate purchase event, as shown in the screenshot below.

[image: 3.4GTM_event_menu.png]

### 3.5 Save the trigger

Give the trigger a clear name, such as Purchase Event , and click Save .

sections.section_heading: Step 4: Install the Kelkoo Sales Tracking tag
sections.content:
### 4.1 Open the Template Gallery

In GTM, select Templates .

Under Tag Templates , click Search Gallery .

[image: 4.1GTM_KST_Tag.png]

### 4.2 Add the Kelkoo Group template

Search for Kelkoo Group Sales Tracking Tag and select it.

In the Template Details window, click Add to workspace .

[image: 4.2GTM_KST_Tag.png]

### 4.3 Create the Kelkoo Sales Tracking tag

Go to Tags and create a new tag.

Under Tag Configuration , select the Kelkoo Group Sales Tracking Tag template.

[image: 4.3GTM_KST_Tag.png]

### 4.4 Configure the tag

Configure the tag using:

- Your Country Code
- Your Merchant ID
- The Order ID GTM variable created in Step 2
- The Order Value GTM variable created in Step 2

Use the variable selector to choose the existing GTM variables created in Steps 2.4 and 2.5. Do not enter their names as plain text.

[image: 4.4GTM_KST_Tag.png]

### 4.5 Add the purchase trigger

Under Triggering , select the custom purchase event trigger created in Step 3.

This ensures that the Kelkoo Sales Tracking tag fires when a purchase is completed.

[image: 4.5GTM_KST_Tag.png]

### 4.6 Save the tag

Click Save .

sections.section_heading: Step 5: Install the Kelkoo Lead Tag
sections.content:
The Kelkoo Lead Tag must also be installed and configured to fire on every page.

### 5.1 Create the Lead Tag

From the Tags menu, create a new Custom HTML tag.

Add the following code:

```
<script async="true" type="text/javascript" src="https://s.kk-resources.com/leadtag.js"></script>
```

Under Triggering , select All Pages .

[image: 5.1GTM_custom_html_lead_tag.png]

[image: 5.2GTM_custom_html_lead_tag.png]

[image: 5.3GTM_custom_html_lead_tag.png]

### 5.2 Save and publish

Save the tag.

Once you have completed the configuration, Preview your GTM container to verify that the tags fire as expected.

When you are satisfied with the setup, publish your GTM changes to complete the Kelkoo Sales Tracking installation.

Once the installation is complete, we strongly recommend testing your implementation to make sure Kelkoo Sales Tracking is working correctly.

See Test your Kelkoo Sales Tracking setup for instructions.
If you experience any issues with your installation, see Troubleshooting GTM Integration before contacting our Support team.

pages.page_title: Manual installation for Kelkoo Sales Tracking

sections.content:
Use this installation method if you are not using Google Tag Manager (GTM) or if you prefer to integrate Kelkoo Sales Tracking directly into your website's source code.

This guide explains how to manually install the two tags required for Kelkoo Sales Tracking:

- Lead Tag – sets a first-party tracking cookie when a user visits your website.
- Conversion Tag – reads the tracking cookie and sends completed order information to Kelkoo.

Important Both the Lead Tag and the Conversion Tag must be installed. Without both tags, Kelkoo Sales Tracking cannot correctly attribute conversions.

Important

Both the Lead Tag and the Conversion Tag must be installed. Without both tags, Kelkoo Sales Tracking cannot correctly attribute conversions.

Before installing the tags, make sure you have:

- Access to your website's source code.
- Your Merchant ID and Country Code .
- Access to the order confirmation (thank-you) page.

sections.section_heading: Find Your Merchant ID and Country Code
sections.content:
Log in to your Kelkoo Merchant Portal and retrieve your Merchant ID and associated Country Code .

These values are required when configuring both tracking tags.

If your website already includes an older version of Kelkoo Sales Tracking, remove it before installing the new tags (search for leadtag.js and _kkstrack ).

Running multiple versions of the tracking code may result in duplicate or incorrect conversion tracking.

The Lead Tag sets the first-party tracking cookie used to attribute future conversions.

Add the following script to every page of your website , immediately before the closing </head> tag.

```
<script async="true" type="text/javascript" src="https://s.kk-resources.com/leadtag.js" ></script>
```

Once installed, the Lead Tag will automatically create the tracking cookie for eligible visitors.

If your website uses a Consent Management Platform (CMP), configure it so that Kelkoo's tracking tags run only after the required user consent has been obtained.

Incorrect CMP configuration may prevent conversions from being attributed correctly.

If conversions are not being tracked correctly, check the following:

- Both tags are installed.
- Only one version of the tracking code is present.
- The Lead Tag loads before the Conversion Tag.
- Dynamic order values are correctly populated.
- Your CMP allows the tags to run after consent is granted.
- The browser console does not report any JavaScript errors.

If the issue persists, contact Kelkoo Support and include:

- your Merchant ID;
- the URL of your order confirmation page (if accessible);
- screenshots or browser console logs where possible.

The tool is structured around 4 sections:

Important! Check regularly that sales are being registered. This is even more important to do after you have implemented updates or changes to your site.

sections.section_heading: In case of issues, check our troubleshooting guide
sections.content: If you are facing issues on the tracking or sales processing part, please have a look at our Common Issues section.

If you face a problem, the first thing to do is to use the Kelkoo Sales Tracking Debugging tool available here .

If this is not sufficient, here is a list of troubleshooting guides for the most common installation methods:

- Troubleshooting GTM Integration
- Troubleshooting Prestashop integration
- Troubleshooting Shopify integration

And if nothing helps, you can directly contact our support team via our contact form and select Subject = "Kelkoo Sales Tracking troubleshooting". Our experienced team will come back to you ASAP.

sections.section_heading: Verify that your GTM makes the correct call
sections.content:
- Go on your Kelkoo Group Merchant Extranet and log into your account then click on the link View your Kelkoo store page in the top right corner of the Home page
- Click on one of your offers to be redirected to your website
- Open "developer console" (usually F12, otherwise right-click on page and "inspect element"), then open "network" tab.
- Check if you have a /gtm call:

[image: TestIntegration5.png]

- Open /gtm call content (usually right-click on call then "open in new tab")
- Check if you find leadtag value in the page
- Check if you find kkstrack value and check that merchantId/country are ok.

### Common Issue 1: Integration has not been published

- Ensure that you have published the integration.

### Common Issue 2: orderId/orderValue fields are undefined when firing Kelkoo Group tag

- Verify that you have removed all existing Kelkoo Group tag
- Re-install from scratch the tag using our brand new GTM template, available here: https://www.kelkoogroup.com/support/merchants-support/google-tag-manager-integration/
- Make sure that variables used for orderId/orderValue fields in template are the good ones: It can be checked in GTM debug mode when doing a fake sale: variables must not be undefined when firing Kelkoo Group tag
- If your variables are undefined it might be because you use Google conversion tag variables, and these variables are pushed in the datalayer below the GTM snippet in confirmation page (see below for more details)
- If the variables are declared after the GTM, then the Firing Trigger must be a Page View - DOM ready trigger instead of All Pages Page View (see below for more details)

### Common Issue 3: datalayer and GTM are not called in the correct order

- If you manually fill the GTM datalayer with the kkstrack script in the source code of the page, integration order is important
- Make sure the datalayer is above the GTM snippet.

Correct datalayer/GTM snippet integration order:

[image: CorrectGTMIntegrationOrder.png]

Incorrect datalayer/GTM snippet integration order:

[image: IncorrectGTMIntegrationOrder.png]

### Common Issue 4: Kelkoo Group Tag not triggered on DOM ready event

- The Kelkoo Group tag must be triggered on DOM ready event, not custom event, to be sure variables are available.
- This has to be checked when you notice that you constantly move back and forth from Kelkoo Sales Tracking V1 to V2 (visible in your Merchant Extranet).

### Common Issue 5: missing or wrong double quotes to declare variable name

- In Google Tag Manager, for a variable to be interpreted it must be put between double brackets :
- For example, do not write 'orderValue': 'dlv_revenue_media' but 'orderValue': '{{dlv_revenue_media}}' **BRACKETS ARE MANDATORY AROUND VALUE **

When you type the opening double brackets, a menu will appear to offer you the list of available variables, in order to avoid typos in the name of the variables

When you type the opening double brackets, a menu will appear to offer you the list of available variables, in order to avoid typos in the name of the variables

- Be sure to use the classic double quote in code; You can sometimes use not well encoded double quotes: you must use " character and not “ character (subtle difference; the second one is utf-8 character https://www.fileformat.info/info/unicode/char/201c/index.htm which must NOT be used) Correct example: {country: "de", merchantId: "100522210"}, {country: "nl", merchantId: "100516712"} Wrong example: {country:“de”,merchantId:“100522210”},{country:“nl”,merchantId:“100516712”}

### Common Issue 6: Tag priority is not correct

- If you use a GTM custom HTML tag, in the Advanced Settings of the tag they must set the priority to 3, so that the tag is fired before the Kelkoo Group Sales Tracking Tag.

{{ amount_no_decimals_with_comma_separator }} | Yes | 1.135 | orderValue: '{{ order.total_price | money_without_currency | remove: '.' }}',

sections.content:

```

```

This has to be removed. In your codebase, it should be generated by this block of code

```
<script type="text/javascript"> var lgtrk_data = { version : "1.3", idshop : "29097548", pt : "purchase", price : "274.92", idp : "20156", qty_idp : "1", price_idp : "274.92" }; (function(a,b,c,d){ a=('https:' == document.location.protocol ? 'https://secure.' : 'http://') + "cimg.leguide.com/js/lgtrk-"+lgtrk_data.version+".min.js"; b=document;c='script';d=b.createElement(c);d.src=a;d.type='text/java'+c;d.async=true; a=b.getElementsByTagName(c)[0];a.parentNode.insertBefore(d,a); })(); </script>
```

Kelkoo Sales Tracking (KST) allows Kelkoo Group to measure the sales generated by the traffic we send to your website.

KST uses a first-party identifier to recognise visits originating from Kelkoo Group and connect them with subsequent purchases. This allows us to measure campaign performance and optimise the traffic we send to you.

sections.section_heading: How does Kelkoo Sales Tracking work?
sections.content:
Kelkoo Sales Tracking uses two main components:

### Lead Tag

The Lead Tag is loaded when a user visits your website after clicking a Kelkoo Group ad.

The Kelkoo click contains a unique identifier in the kk URL parameter. The Lead Tag retrieves this identifier and, when the required consent has been obtained, stores it using first-party browser storage.

Because the identifier is stored on your website's domain rather than on a Kelkoo Group domain, it is considered first-party .

The stored identifier allows KST to recognise the original Kelkoo visit if the user returns to your website and completes a purchase later.

### Conversion Tag

The Conversion Tag fires whenever an order is completed.

It sends the transaction information required by Kelkoo Group, such as:

- the Order ID;
- the Order Value;
- the Kelkoo identifier, when available;
- additional transaction information, depending on your implementation.

The Sales Tracking Tag should fire for every completed order , regardless of the traffic source responsible for the user's final visit.

Kelkoo Group then applies its attribution logic to determine whether the transaction should be attributed to Kelkoo traffic.

[image: NonTechnicalKSTView.png]

Kelkoo Sales Tracking uses a Kelkoo Channel Last Click attribution model with a 30-day conversion window .

### How does attribution work?

When a user clicks a Kelkoo Group ad, KST stores the identifier associated with that visit.

If the same user completes a purchase within the following 30 days, the sale can be attributed to Kelkoo Group.

This remains the case if the user returns to your website through another channel before completing the purchase.

For example:

Day 1: User clicks a Kelkoo Group ad → visits your website → does not purchase

Day 5: User returns through an organic Google search → does not purchase

Day 10: User returns directly to your website → completes a purchase

In this example, Kelkoo Sales Tracking attributes the sale to Kelkoo Group , because the user clicked through Kelkoo within the previous 30 days.

Important Kelkoo Sales Tracking attribution differs from the attribution used by Google Analytics or other analytics platforms. For example, an analytics platform using a cross-channel last-click model may attribute the transaction above to another channel, while KST attributes it to Kelkoo Group. These differences do not necessarily indicate a tracking issue; they simply result from different attribution methodologies.

Important

Kelkoo Sales Tracking attribution differs from the attribution used by Google Analytics or other analytics platforms.

For example, an analytics platform using a cross-channel last-click model may attribute the transaction above to another channel, while KST attributes it to Kelkoo Group.

These differences do not necessarily indicate a tracking issue; they simply result from different attribution methodologies.

The KST conversion window is 30 days .

A transaction can therefore be attributed to Kelkoo Group when it occurs within 30 days of a qualifying Kelkoo click.

After the 30-day period has expired, that click is no longer considered for attribution.

If another Kelkoo click occurs during the conversion window, the most recent qualifying Kelkoo click is used.

For more information about differences between KST and analytics platforms, see Understanding Differences Between KelkooGroup Reported Clicks in Google Analytics 4 .

Tag Loading: Does your technology require the tags to be loaded only once for SPAs, or should they fire with each new virtual page view?

Our lead tag is used to store the user id from the kk query parameter to a first party cookie. The goal of this is the correct attribution and measurement of the sales. It need to be loaded only once.

Performance: We've noticed that the tags inject into the head section with each virtual page load, potentially affecting site performance. Do you have guidelines for minimizing this impact?

The tag does indeed load a pixel asynchronously as a fallback to store the user id. As this is asynchronous this does not impact site performance.

Optimization: Are there specific measures or best practices you recommend for ensuring accurate and optimized tracking for SPAs? Additionally, are any changes or alterations to pixel codes necessary for SPA compatibility?

There is no optimization needed for SPAs, as we don't track the individual pages of products viewed by the end user. We do not use this tag for retargeting purpose.
